questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How safe driverless cars are compared with human drivers
How to plan for your retirement
Different attitudes to risk and what our brains show
Why bungee jumping is dangerous
questions.why: Neil says the topic is risk and how different people react to it; they discuss brain research on risk.

questions.q: What does Rob say about his bungee jump in New Zealand?
options: He loved it so much that he wants to do it again soon
He didn't really enjoy it and won't do it again
He was too scared to jump
He did it for charity
questions.why: Rob says 'Not really, no. I won't do it again!'

questions.q: Why wouldn't Rob go in a driverless car?
options: They are too expensive
He gets car sick when someone else is driving him
He prefers cycling
He doesn't trust anybody's driving, even a computer's
questions.why: Rob says 'I don't trust anybody's driving - even a computer.'

questions.q: How many types of attitude to risk does Joe Kable describe?
options: Three
Two
Four
Five
questions.why: Rob says 'there were three': risk-averse, risk-tolerant and risk-seeking.

options: Risk seekers are more intelligent
Brains differ between people who avoid risk and accept it
Everyone's brain reacts to risk in the same way
Brain scans are too risky to use on people who are afraid of risk
questions.why: Neil says he found differences in brain structure between risk-averse and risk-tolerant people.

questions.q: Who does Kable say would find this knowledge useful?
options: Doctors
Car makers
Financial advisors
Sports coaches
questions.why: He says it's exactly what financial advisors want to assess when you save for retirement.

questions.q: Why would a financial advisor want to know your attitude to risk?
options: To decide how much money to charge you for their advice
To sell you insurance
To decide if you can retire early
To help decide what to do with your savings
questions.why: Rob says it would help them assess what to do with your money, for example for retirement.

questions.q: What does Rob suggest his financial planner could do instead of a brain scan?
options: Simply ask him how he feels about risk
Look carefully at his bank account and spending
Ask his friends about him
Give him a written test
questions.why: Rob says his planner 'could just ask me about how I feel about risk rather than giving me a brain scan'.
